item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I dunno, in previous installments, the memeage was cringeworthy, but I'm started to like Thorn's naivete. Not, mind, that this should be taken as carte blanche to go over 9000 with the memes. It's more the narration that I would say needs tightening.

item.title: Pretty good
item.content:encoded:
I liked this as a whole, but I think I spotted some typos/grammar bugs:

With wave of the arm, whole rows of crystalline pews upturned by sheer force as pages and pages of carrier wave hymnals scattered in the air.

So! You guys look like you are having a good time. Who'd ever had known that a couple of chippers would be so fun.

Grape was for sure they were about to be found out as he watched Thorn fold like cardboard.

Ah. Well I'd love to rattle off some more racing tips, for you guys but I'd like to attend that vigil tonight.

These might be intentional, or not. Either way I am looking forward to more.
+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I took "chipper" to mean a person whose only implant is a chip in their brain that lets them access cyberspace, as opposed to a more integrated member who may have many extensive modifications.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have to agree with some of the previous comments. The writing here makes me cringe a few more times than it ought to, especially with references like "Gotta go fast."

Still, I was entertained enough, especially with the entrance of hatbot. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Ah, Skynet. The habit of naming AI-related things after it in homage to Terminator has made it pretty likely that when an AI finally does try to wipe out humanity, it will be called Skynet.

Also, I'm a little unclear on what "chipper" means here. Is it a type of person?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hatbot was a chatbot with (bad) learning and conversation software, which led to often hilarious and distracting non sequiturs, which led to the -j, and the Mann Incident.

All the AI's in this series are based on previous or present chatbots.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The writing continues to be not-great, but I'm still enjoying the heck out of this.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I'll just pipe in here. I actually tried to avoid site in-jokes with hatbot's introduction and as far as I'm concerned the only pre-existing canon on Hatbot I'm considering is Mann's original tale, The Hatbot Chronicles. The -J or other in-jokes about him are pretty much excluded from this canon.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hmm. I definitely like this better than the other installments (perhaps in part because it put more emphasis on characters I like better). For me at least, that ending didn't have much payoff, as references to site injokes rarely have dramatic value. Others may disagree on that point.

All in all, it's pretty good. For now, I'm going to novote, but there's a good chance I'll upvote upon further consideration.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I assume that Hatbot is the Gen IV AI that the Foundation doesn't discuss? After all, who would want to admit that they created a Zalgo-level entity.
